title: inbox\settings.json schema 4 (R1): Linux heavy and light tier counts, Windows count, per-profile shares, host reserve
x-owner: R1 step 1 (contract); R1 step 3 (supervisor reader); R1 step 4 (tray writer). Schema 3 stays the live contract until the supervisor lists 4 in status.v5.json settings_schemas

linux_backend.description: Supervisor-side; the tray writes back what status.v5.json reports and never changes it. Flipped only by the cutover item P27. Default wsl-legacy.

linux_light_count.description: Light tier slots (labels self-hosted,linux,x64,fresh,light): reservation 1 CPU / 3 GiB, hard cap 4 CPU / 8 GiB each (docs/ROADMAP.md R1).

linux_heavy_count.description: Heavy tier slots (labels self-hosted,linux,x64,fresh,heavy): reservation 8 CPU / 20 GiB each, may burst to the pool, 4x CPU weight.

windows_runner_count.description: 0..5; not counted against the Linux tiers.

job_cpus.description: Windows runners only in schema 4 (the Linux per-slot limits come from the tier table, not from settings); same range as schema 3.

lease_wall_clock_hours.description: Host cap per VM lease, default 6. Past it a quarantined slot whose runner GitHub reports offline is destroyed; a runner GitHub reports busy is never destroyed, only flagged in status.
